Soojin / team — attached is v2 of the topology with annotations. High-level points to include in the attestation: 
- Control plane is a Redwood-managed service in our control region; for Private deployments customers may elect a private control plane deployment where API control traffic is routed over a customer-managed VPC peering connection.
- Data plane for Dedicated is in a dedicated GPU pool; network namespaces, per-tenant KV cache partitioning and hypervisor-level encryption are used to reduce blast radius.
- For Private (VPC) we deploy a sidecar model where inference nodes exist in the customer's VPC and all egress flows can be restricted to customer NAT or our optional egress-proxy (static IP pool available on request).
- KMS: customer-managed KMS is supported for model keys and customer secrets (bring-your-own-KMS via Cloud KMS/HSM integration). We also offer Redwood-managed KMS for convenience.
- Egress: default behavior is SNAT through provider-managed NAT; to support firewall allowlists we can either (a) reserve static egress IPs for the customer's Dedicated pool, or (b) recommend VPC peering with forced-tunnel egress to the customer's NAT gateway.

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-private-topology-v2.drawio.png (annotated, 420KB)

I left some open questions in the diagram callouts (noted with orange flags) about third-party telemetry endpoints Greenleaf might require and whether Greenleaf wants an airgapped on-prem window for model updates.
